bug_semantics: Traefik's Kubernetes CRD provider treats crossProviderNamespaces as an allowlist for which namespaces may emit cross-provider references from IngressRoute, IngressRouteTCP, IngressRouteUDP, and TraefikService. HTTP service serversTransport names containing '@' are rejected unless the parent namespace is on that list (makeServersTransportKey). IngressRouteTCP service serversTransport names go through makeTCPServersTransportKey, which returns a qualified name such as foo@file after only the older AllowCrossNamespace/@kubernetescrd suffix check. A low-privileged CRD author in a namespace omitted from the allowlist can therefore force Traefik to store LoadBalancer.ServersTransport="foo@file" and, at dial time, apply that file-provider TCPServersTransport's mTLS client certificates, SPIFFE identity, or PROXY-protocol settings. CWE-863 incorrect authorization; the HTTP sibling proves the intended gate.
flaw_origin: The CVE is an incomplete authorization control, not the original TCP ServersTransport feature. git log -L shows makeTCPServersTransportKey (including the '@' passthrough) was first written in 3eeea2bb2bfb49e2e0adbd77e65d45183796b111 (2022-12-09, 'Add TCP Servers Transports support') as a copy of the then-HTTP makeServersTransportKey, which also returned qualified names without an allowlist because none existed. The security invariant was created in GitHub PR 13094: member 982f10368ffe22ee681dc1f9a9a4d5f564ebfbfb (2026-04-29) first added isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed to HTTP makeServersTransportKey and to IngressRouteTCP TLS-option and TCP-middleware references, while documenting ServersTransports as in-scope. makeTCPServersTransportKey did not exist on that v2.11 tree, so the TCP serversTransport path never received the new gate. GitHub squash-merged the PR as 28604083a41b6d6e8c206d71e0bce464bff1edb7 (identical tree to PR tip 73d0949d446a09f02f6dd30cc5968c47640100c4) with description text covering IngressRouteTCP. Merge 8c7634bcde599dd14d4d5c1346acd734f3a007a1 (v2.11 into v3.6; parents v3.6.16 801eb2f149fb0d50cfa706abb741a1c0ae4c7800 and the squash) is the first tagged v3.6 tree that has both the allowlist and the unchecked TCP key builder; the function body was unchanged versus v3.6.16. Vendor GHSA affected range starts at v3.6.17 / v3.7.1, matching that landing, not v3.0. Follow-up PR 13458 states it aligns TCP serversTransport with the HTTP check that 13094 added.

reasoning: The live vulnerability is CWE-863: after CrossProviderNamespaces became the documented IngressRouteTCP allowlist, HTTP serversTransport references were gated and TCP serversTransport references were not, so foo@file from a non-allowlisted namespace is accepted and consumed by pkg/tcp DialerManager. CVE-2026-65602 is PUBLISHED on CVE.org; the GitHub advisory is not withdrawn. The 2022 commit 3eeea2bb2 first wrote the TCP '@' passthrough, but at that time HTTP used the same pattern and no allowlist existed, so those lines were not a policy bypass; vendor affected versions start only when PR 13094 landed (v3.6.17 / v3.7.1). The BIC is therefore the smallest reconstructable commit that first wrote the incomplete control: PR 13094 member 982f10368ffe22ee681dc1f9a9a4d5f564ebfbfb, whose parent ee94dc53 lacks CrossProviderNamespaces, isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed, and makeTCPServersTransportKey. That member added the HTTP serversTransport allowlist and TCP TLS/middleware gates on v2.11, where TCP serversTransport did not exist. GitHub squash 2860408 is the surviving tagged object (same tree as PR tip 73d0949) and is not used as BIC. Merge 8c7634bcde is the v3.6 backport that first combined the allowlist with the pre-existing TCP key builder; it is a merge, not a first-write, and did not change makeTCPServersTransportKey. Fix 67501cb on v3.6 (also in v3.7.7) inserts the missing isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed call.
